overview: This Senate resolution designates May 11 through May 17, 2025, as National Police Week. It honors federal, state, local and tribal law enforcement officers, lists by name the 234 officers killed in the line of duty in 2024, and notes FBI figures showing 18 more killed in early 2025. It expresses support for officers, recognizes the need to give them the equipment, training and resources to stay safe, offers condolences to the families of fallen officers, and encourages the public to honor law enforcement during the week. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 13, 2025.
for: Supporters say it honors officers who died serving their communities and supports the families they left behind.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it recognizes officers' needs for equipment and training but does not change any law or provide funding.
